inspection.basis: Independently observed original PNG pixels, not the raw SVG or another modern candidate.
inspection.coordinateConvention: Approximate source screen x,y, top-left origin. Pixel positions are observations, not apparatus dimensions.

groups.description: One tall horseshoe magnet arches above two unequal-looking legs in oblique projection. The darker far/left leg descends around x70-145 to y340-375. The broad right leg runs around x190-275 down to y448-465; its inner lower face projects into the gap. The top connects both legs. Smooth curved edges and the right-side depth face are visible.

An N-shaped pole mark is legible at approximately x173-187,y390-416 on the inner lower right magnet face. A pale curved mark on the far/left terminal is not sufficiently clear to transcribe. Preserve the supported N only; do not assign S by inference.
groups.unresolved: Left pole glyph: no reliable letter asserted; source polarity is not swapped.

groups.description: A tilted rectangular multi-turn wire frame occupies the lower gap, with closely spaced wire runs on its upper sloping side near x95-183,y326-349 and lower/right portions near x99-174,y390-425. The upper edge slopes up toward the right. A dark small top face near x80-165,y296-330 belongs to the far terminal region and must not replace the wire frame. Parts of the wire/terminal junctions overlap and are obscured. Several turns are supported by both prose and pixels; the raster does not determine an exact integer winding count.
groups.unresolved: Exact turn count, hidden corner details and hidden electrical junctions are not invented.

groups.description: An axle extends left from the rotating frame toward the ring assembly. Its projection is almost horizontal, rising slightly rightward from approximately x29,y403 toward the frame around x126,y379. The axle is mechanical, not an electrical wire.

Two separate ring-like contact zones surround the leftward axle, one around x29-50,y389-421 and another around x61-84,y385-411. Their outlines are elliptical/cylindrical in projection. Smaller brush/contact strokes touch their lower margins. Additional dark shaft/collar structure occurs to their right. These are visible source shapes, not proof of either a slip-ring or split-commutator netlist.
groups.unresolved: Ring continuity, insulation, segmentation and coil-terminal assignment cannot be read reliably. No device subtype is labelled.

groups.description: A short curved rotation arrow is just left of the axle/rings near x12-26,y383-423. Its pointed upper-left end is retained as an upward-directed tangent in that local projection; no global clockwise or counterclockwise viewpoint is claimed.

Two leads descend separately from the lower contact region. The left lead starts near x50,y414 and curls down through about x74,y463 toward x100,y504. The right starts near x86,y414 and descends/curls toward x138,y495. Neither returns to the other or to a drawn meter. Keep both disconnected free ends, as shown.

One apparatus, no panels, grid, axes, tick values, measured geometry, numerical givens, meter, load, return wire, magnetic-field arrows or current arrows. No caption or cultural decoration occurs in this cropped PNG. The full bilingual lesson discusses the conditional closed-circuit galvanometer response; that prose must remain bound without adding a galvanometer to the image.

modernAdditions: Fresh smooth deterministic horseshoe surfaces and perspective frame edges; no scan pixels or traced scan texture are used as a modern layer.
Piecewise vertical composition enlarges the lower apparatus while retaining the tall arch, oblique frame, leftward axle, contacts, local arrow direction and hanging free leads.
Three distinct visible winding runs illustrate the text's several turns. Three is not claimed as an exact recovered winding count; hidden returns and terminal netlist are omitted.
English component callouts Magnet, Coil, Axle, Contacts and Leads, with thin undirected leaders. N is the only recovered source pole glyph.
Semantic color roles only; no conventional red/blue pole coloring, B vector, current arrows, meter or external closed circuit.
metricLimits: The original has no given lengths or angles. Exact authored coordinates and executable constraints define a stable instructional projection, not measured dimensions extracted from the scan.
